Job Details:
Job Description:
The Role and Impact
Intel's Client AI Architecture team is seeking an Deep Learning Hardware Engineer to help shape future generations of Intel's Neural Processing Unit (NPU) architecture for AI PCs, Edge AI, Agentic AI, Physical AI, and multimodal foundation models.
In this role, you will work at the intersection of AI, computer architecture, and hardware-software co-design to optimize AI workloads and drive innovations in next-generation AI acceleration technologies. You will collaborate with architecture, software, compiler, and machine learning teams to develop high-performance, power-efficient AI solutions for Intel client platforms.
The ideal candidate has experience developing, optimizing, or deploying AI workloads on NPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, or related computing architectures. Experience with Intel NPUs, OpenVINO, AI software stacks, compiler technologies, AI inference optimization, and hardware-software co-design is highly desirable.
What You’ll Do
Key responsibilities will include but not limited to:
Contribute to the design and optimization of neural compute and AI accelerator architectures.
Develop and evaluate RTL implementations of hardware features supporting machine learning workloads.
Analyze AI models and workloads to identify performance, power, and efficiency opportunities.
Partner with architecture, software, and algorithm teams to define future hardware capabilities.
Support hardware-software co-design efforts to optimize AI solutions across the technology stack.
Evaluate neural network mapping strategies for accelerated inference execution.
Apply optimization techniques such as quantization, compression, pruning, and sparsity to improve AI efficiency.
Utilize computer architecture principles including pipelining, parallelism, memory hierarchy, and data movement optimization.
Participate in technical innovation activities, including invention disclosures, patents, conference papers, and publications.

Behavioral traits that we are looking for:
Curiosity & Learning Agility – Eager to learn new technologies, quickly absorb concepts, and continuously develop technical expertise.
Problem Solving – Uses analytical thinking to break down complex challenges and develop practical, data-driven solutions.
Collaboration – Works effectively across diverse teams, values different perspectives, and builds strong working relationships.
Ownership & Initiative – Takes responsibility for deliverables, follows through on commitments, and proactively identifies opportunities for improvement.
Adaptability – Thrives in a fast-paced environment, embraces change, and adjusts priorities as business needs evolve.
Communication – Clearly communicates technical concepts, ideas, and recommendations to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Innovation Mindset – Demonstrates creativity, challenges assumptions, and seeks new approaches to improve products, processes, and customer outcomes.

Intel invests in our people and offers a complete and competitive package of benefits employees and their families through every stage of life.
See Intel Benefits for more details.

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Requirements listed would be obtained through a combination of industry relevant job experience, internship experiences and or schoolwork/classes/research.

Minimum Qualifications and Experience:
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a STEM-related field with 3+ years of relevant experience; OR Master's degree in the same fields with 2+ years of experience; OR PhD degree in the same fields with 3+ months of educational or work experience.

Your experience described above must be in the following:
Digital Logic Design and RTL Design using System Verilog or Verilog.
AI model architectures, layers, activation functions, and neural network topologies (e.g., Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Pi0.5).
Experience working with Git workflows and repositories.
Optimizing AI models for performance, such as quantization, pruning, and compression.

Preferred Qualifications and Experience:
Familiarity with AI frameworks, neural computing operations, and hardware-accelerated inference techniques.
Hands-on experience with modern deep learning topologies, including foundational models.
In-depth knowledge of computer architecture concepts such as multi-core/multi-threading, memory hierarchy, and floating-point vs. fixed-point computations.
Experience collaborating in cross-disciplinary teams to align hardware and software requirements.

Why Join Us
The Client Computing Group (CCG) develops industry-leading technologies that power personal computing experiences around the world. Within Intel's AI Hardware Engineering organization, you'll help build the neural compute technologies that drive future AI-enabled PCs and intelligent computing platforms.

This role provides opportunities to:
Work on cutting-edge AI and machine learning technologies.
Learn from industry-leading hardware and AI experts.
Influence next-generation AI silicon architecture.
Collaborate across hardware, software, and research teams.

As a Post Launch Production Program Manager, you will play a pivotal role in driving the success of manufacturing operations within Intel's Central Engineering Group. You will lead cross-functional teams, manage schedules, oversee project deliverables, and ensure operational efficiency to maintain production and maximize revenue/margins. Your ability to manage complex projects and ensure seamless collaboration across teams will directly contribute to delivering world-class technology solutions to our customers.

The Central Engineering Group (CEG) is at the core of Intel's innovation, focused on delivering exceptional engineering and manufacturing solutions. As part of the Networking Platforms Operation (NPO) Manufacturing Operations organization, this team works across multiple disciplines to support Intel's technological advancements and broader corporate goals. Joining this group means being part of a collaborative environment that values precision, innovation, and the drive to push boundaries in the industry.
NPO is an exciting and critical board design, validation, and manufacturing team responsible for providing and supporting Ethernet products and technology. As part of the NPO Team, you would be joining a mature team that has been productizing and selling Ethernet products for years and will continue to deliver world-class products that are extensively tested for network interoperability, reliability, and performance.

Strong ability to multi-task and manage several activities at once.

Job Description:
At Intel, we create world-changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet. This position is part of Intel's Advanced Packaging Technology Manufacturing (APTM) division, which is responsible for the development and commercialization of industry-leading semiconductor packaging technologies for mobile, edge, and hyperscale computing platforms. Within APTM, our Assembly Technology Development (ATD) team pioneers innovative package assembly solutions and scales them for high-volume manufacturing.
We are seeking a Packaging Module Development Engineer to join our campus in Chandler, Arizona. In this role, you will contribute to advancing technology and foundry capabilities by developing advanced thermal interface and warpage mitigation solutions. This role sits at the cutting edge of materials science and mechanical engineering, where you will innovate next-generation materials, qualify specialized assembly equipment, and collaborate with global teams to optimize assembly processes for quality, yield, and high-volume manufacturability.
Key Responsibilities:

Thermal & Warpage Engineering: Develop, qualify, and implement thermal interface and warpage mitigation solutions to support future packaging platforms.
Assembly Process Optimization: Partner with cross-functional, matrixed teams to optimize advanced assembly processes for quality, reliability, cost, yield, productivity, and high-volume scalability.
Material & Fabrication Innovation: Research and qualify next-generation materials, equipment, and fabrication processes to enhance packaging capabilities at scale.
Project Management: Manage engineering project milestones to meet critical technology development and product timelines.
Technical Problem Solving: Apply statistical methods, structural judgment, and materials analysis to resolve complex packaging assembly failures.
Sustaining & High-Volume Support: Provide sustaining engineering support for equipment performance and process health inside high-volume manufacturing lines.
Foundry Customer Engagement: Respond directly to foundry customer technical requests and resolve process integration events promptly.

As a Successful Candidate, You Will Bring:

Technical Leadership & Strategic Planning: Outstanding critical thinking skills with a natural aptitude for coaching, developing, and leading technical teams.
Tolerance for Ambiguity & Adaptability: Excellent flexibility in managing changing priorities, fluctuating timelines, and dynamic environment demands.
Collaborative Influencing: Strong interpersonal skills to effectively align priorities across highly matrixed, cross-organizational business units.
Initiative & Autonomy: Driven self-starter with the focus to drive complex research initiatives independently.
Apply today to join Intel Arizona's Assembly Technology Development team. Partner with global industry leaders, take ownership of advanced thermal and structural breakthroughs, and build a rewarding engineering career.
Qualifications:
This is an entry level position and will be compensated accordingly. You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Relevant experience can be obtained through schoolwork, classes and project work, internships, military training, and/or work experience.

A Master’s Degree or a PhD in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Applied Physics, or a related STEM field.

1+ years of experience in materials characterization, packaging process development, or mechanical testing (obtained through academic research, coursework, internships, or industry experience).

At least one publication as a primary or contributing author in a peer-reviewed technical journal.
Preferred Qualifications:

1+ years of experience:
Semiconductor packaging technology development, including hands-on application of Statistical Process Control (SPC) or Design of Experiments (DOE).
Executing complex, time-critical engineering projects within a semiconductor foundry or manufacturing environment.
Utilizing Python, MATLAB, or SQL to analyze multi-dimensional engineering datasets.

People come to work at Microchip because we help design the technology that runs the world. They stay because our culture supports their growth and stability. Visit our careers page to see what exciting opportunities and company perks await!
Job Description:
Join the Design Engineering team as an Engineer II—Design, responsible for compute-in-memory neural network modeling and algorithm implementation. Support architecture development, RTL and circuit design, integration, verification, performance, power, area, documentation, and the product lifecycle.

In this role, you will independently execute defined assignments, partner with relevant technical and business stakeholders, and help deliver reliable, high-quality engineering outcomes while driving continuous improvement.

Responsibilities:

Develop neural network models for architectures such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), transformers, large language models (LLMs), and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for analog compute-in-memory (ACIM) systems.
Model variation and mismatch across ACIM components.
Model the power, performance, and area (PPA) of ACIM solutions.
Implement ACIM algorithms.
Contribute to ACIM hardware architecture development.
Coordinate with engineers across design, technology, process, and test teams to advance ACIM technology.
Translate product specifications, neural network performance targets, and schedule needs into design requirements and plans.
Analyze specifications, simulations, timing, power, area, integration, risks, dependencies, and technical trade-offs for ACIM solutions.
Requirements/Qualifications:
Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Physics, or a related field.
2.5–5 years of experience or research in neural network modeling for compute-in-memory or neuromorphic computing.
Knowledge of neural network architectures, such as multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), gated recurrent units (GRUs), CNNs, and small language models (sLLMs).
Experience with neural network modeling for compute-in-memory systems.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Successful candidates are expected to demonstrate:

Reliability, accountability, and a record of sustained contributions in prior roles.
Effective teamwork and cross-functional collaboration.
Integrity and accuracy when representing qualifications, experience, and credentials.

Preferred Qualifications:

PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
Experience with RISC-V architecture.
Knowledge of nonvolatile memory technologies.
Knowledge of VLSI design flows.
Knowledge of computer architecture.
Experience with validation, debugging, and testing.
Experience with CAD and design tools, such as HSPICE/HSIM, Verilog, and Cadence Design Entry.
Knowledge of programming and scripting languages, such as Python, Tcl, C++, or SystemC.
Knowledge of semiconductor device physics.

Feeling, Hearing, Seeing, Talking, Works Alone, Works Around Others

As the global leader in high-speed connectivity, Ciena builds the critical infrastructure powering the AI era. We’re a technology company shaping the future of networking, guided by innovation, integrity, and collaboration. Through development opportunities, meaningful work, and flexibility, Ciena supports growth and well-being—on and off the job. Connect with a career that matters.

Ciena's New Product Introduction team is seeking a highly motivated test development engineer to join their dynamic team. This role involves playing a key part in delivering cutting-edge automated calibration and verification solutions for Ciena's optical portfolio, with a primary focus on Ciena's Wavelogic Extreme high-performance coherent modems.
We are seeking an exceptional candidate who exemplifies a strong technical acumen and a data-driven problem-solving approach. This individual should demonstrate proficiency in troubleshooting hardware and software-related issues with expertise and precision. Effective and concise communication skills are vital, as the candidate will be responsible for effectively conveying their work to diverse teams, including designers, product engineers, contract manufacturers, and operators. The role encompasses a broad spectrum of responsibilities, ranging from selecting test station instruments to developing automation code for both hardware and software components.
As part of the job requirements, regular attendance at the office is necessary on a daily basis. Additionally, there may be occasional evening meetings that you will need to attend
Primary Responsibilities
Develop and support test automation for both new and existing production lines
Support the R&D team with test tools during the prototype development
Support the contract manufacturer partners in testing beta prototypes, pre-production, and high-volume production
Analyze production statistics to improve test time and yields as production scales
Support failure analysis, root cause identification and corrective action implementation of components, sub-system, and field failures
Facilitate the smooth transfer of new products to high-volume production across multiple sites.
Develop and document fault isolation troubleshooting tools and guides
Required Skills
Must Have
Bachelor’s degree in Electrical/Optical Engineering, Physics or Computer Science
Experience using optical and radio frequency RF test equipment (spectrum analyzers, oscilloscopes, power meters, attenuators)
3+ years test automation software development (C#, Python, or Matlab)
A comprehensive understanding of the fundamental components of high speed modems such as CDMs (coherent driver-modulators), intradyne coherent-receivers (ICRs), semiconductor lasers and amplifiers, tunable filters, and others.
Good understanding of statistics in a production environment (CPk analysis, paretos)
Preferred
Test engineering experience including offshore production and debug management
Experience using source control tools such as git
Experience using the Atlassian suite of tools (Bitbucket/Sourcetree/Jira/Confluence)
Ability to travel up to 10% of the time outside of Canada
Fluency in oral and written French is desirable
